brief: Tonight is Legs A, and it is the same Legs A card you did not use yesterday. Nothing has been logged since Pull A on 18 August, so almost nothing has moved — that is deliberate, not laziness. Re-deriving numbers from evidence that has not changed is how you end up with a different card every morning for no reason. One thing did change, and it changed in your favour: yesterday's card was written for a man walking into his sixth straight training day, one day after four deadlift sets topping 255 for six. You rested instead. That fatigue is gone, so the discount that went with it is gone too. The leg press is the only lift that moves. It stays at three sets and the top set stays 240 for eight — after eighteen days away from this session the heaviest set is not where you go looking for answers — but the two lighter sets get their reps back: 180 for ten, then 220 for nine. Eight on all three was an exact copy of the first three sets you did on 2 August, which asks nothing of you. The second change is that the recovery trainer withdrew its own veto on the Bulgarian split squats. Yesterday it wanted them cut and I overruled it; today it says plainly that its only grounds were the six-day streak and the deadlifts, both of which the rest day killed, and it will not go looking for a new reason to keep an old conclusion. So they run as written, three sets at 17.5 in each hand. It still wants you watched: you have never taken this lift past two sets, so the third set is the whole point, and if you actually wobble rather than just burn, stop the lift there instead of shaving reps. Weaker leg first, then match it with the stronger one — never beat it. Everything else is yesterday's card unchanged: leg curls 127.5 then 142.5 twice, extensions 150 twice, hips 105 and 135, calves 300, crunches 60, hanging leg raises for thirteen. On conditioning, you have a rest day banked and a short session ahead — twelve to fifteen minutes of steady cardio after you rack the last set costs you nothing tonight and you are eleven weeks from the point where it stops being optional.

flags.note: Yesterday's Legs A never happened — nothing was logged on 19 August. You rested, and tonight is that same session. Nothing new has been logged since 18 August, so tonight's numbers are yesterday's card on purpose, with one lift changed.

The leg press is the one change. Because the rest day happened, the two lighter sets get their reps back: 180 for ten and 220 for nine, instead of eight on all three. The top set stays 240 for eight and it is still three sets, not four.

The recovery trainer withdrew its own veto on the Bulgarian split squats. Its words: the only grounds were the six-day streak and the deadlifts, and the rest day killed both. They run tonight, three sets at 17.5. If you wobble rather than just burn on the third set, stop the lift there — that is still its call.

Open question for you, and I cannot put it on a card. Since you came back the rotation has run Push A, Pull B, Legs B, Push A, Pull A — Push A twice in four days, while Push B has not run since 3 August and Legs A not since 2 August. That is the day the rotation resumes from, not the plan itself, and only you can move it in Settings.

Answering something you asked on 2 August and never got a reply to: no, three sets of hanging leg raises was not right. Your third set that day fell to ten. It was cut to two sets on 3 August and the rep range widened on the 17th, but nobody told you that was your question being answered.

One of tonight's cards asks to move a leg-curl set off Legs B and onto Legs A. On 18 August I told you four sets on Legs B is right, and no Legs B has been logged since, so that answer stands — this is a different question, whether that fourth set is better spent on Legs A. It is your call and No is a real answer.

Your corrective question from 17 August, finished off: face pulls went back onto Pull A and Pull B on the 18th and the hip abductor back onto Legs B. Tonight's fourth card is the last missing piece — the hip adductor was never put back beside it, so the outside of your hip is worked twice a cycle and the inside once.

Still open, and I still cannot card it: your core work is all spinal flexion, and there is no anti-rotation movement anywhere in the app's exercise list, so a Pallof press cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.

Three rows in your recent log are substitutions you made when machines were taken — the triceps machine on 17 August, dumbbell hammer curls on the 18th, plus a set of cable door hinges you added yourself. Those numbers are not being read as loads for the prescribed machines.
Your deadlift beat the card on 18 August: 255 for six, twice, against an ask of 245. Next Pull A opens at 255.
Meso 1 closes on 23 August and Meso 2 opens on the 24th. There is no back-off week in between — the 14 August panel dropped it on the grounds that the 4-13 August layoff had already shed the fatigue.

proposals.why: On all three Legs A nights your first leg-press set has been a build-up - 160, 160 and 180 against top sets of 220, 220 and 240 - so the four sets the plan asks for are really three of work plus a ramp, and at three minutes of rest each this is the most expensive slot on your longest session; tonight's card already runs three, and this makes it the standing shape.

Legs A gives the front of your leg nine sets - leg press, split squats and extensions - against three of leg curl and no hinge at all, and on 2 August all three of those curl sets finished at the top of the range at 135 for fifteen, so this makes it four; the card below takes that same set off Legs B, so your week's hamstring total does not move.

Read this one carefully: on 18 August I answered your written question by telling you four sets on Legs B is right, and no Legs B has been logged since, so nothing new has happened - this is the program trainer asking a different question, whether that fourth set is better spent on Legs A where you have nine quad sets and no hinge at all, rather than on the one day you already deadlift-pattern with RDLs. Accepting moves the set; declining keeps four on Legs B exactly as I told you, and No is a real answer.

Legs B just got the hip abductor back but not its partner, so the outside of your hip is now worked twice a cycle and the inside only once - this puts the adductor back beside it on your heavy hinge day, two sets of twelve to fifteen, the way you ran the pair on Legs B last winter.

dissent.progression: Put the reps back on the two lighter sets - 180 for ten and 220 for nine - because the eights were only discounted for a sixth straight training day that never happened.
dissent.recovery: Hold yesterday's card at 180, 220 and 240 for eight - no new data has been logged, so no number should move.
dissent.why: Recovery is right as a general rule and I follow it on the other eight lifts tonight: nothing has been logged since 18 August, so nothing else moved. But this lift is the exception the rule is not built for. Yesterday's eights were not a reading of what he can press - they were a discount, and the printed reason on his card said so in words: day six of a streak, one day after four deadlift sets. He rested. That reason is now false, and leaving the number up while its own stated justification has evaporated would put a lie on the card. Recovery itself refused to defend the eights on their merits - it wrote that it does not block the restore and that ten at 180 is nowhere near his limit, having pressed 180 for twelve, eleven and ten on the high-foot leg press on 16 August. So this is not a seat overruled, it is a seat declining to write a number it does not actually believe. I took progression's version whole and left the 240 top set untouched, because eighteen days away from this session is a real fact and the heaviest set is the wrong place to test it. Recovery's one hard line - three sets, not four - I upheld, and its explicit trade was that restoring the fourth leg-press set would cost the split squat's third; I restored neither set, so that trade was never triggered.

overrides.reason: Three sets tonight, not four - your first set has always been a build-up. Yesterday's card asked eight reps on all three, which is exactly the first three sets you already did on 2 August, and it asked that because you were heading into a sixth straight training day. You rested instead, so the two lighter sets get their reps back: ten at 180, nine at 220. The top set stays 240 for eight - eighteen days away from this session is not the time to push the heaviest one.

The recovery trainer withdrew its veto on this lift, so it runs as written. Both times it has run you logged only two sets and topped out at nine reps, so the card asking three sets of ten at 17.5 is a target you have never come close to. Weight holds; the reps are set so all three sets finish, because finishing the third set is the actual progress. Weaker leg first, then match it. If you wobble rather than just burn, stop the lift there.

You finished all three sets at the top of the range on 2 August at 120, 135 and 135 for fifteen, which pays for the 7.5-lb step, and you have already carried 142.5 for four sets of twelve on 16 August - so restarting at 135 would be redoing work you have done. Thirteen at 142.5 is the step; the hamstring rest comes from three sets tonight instead of four.

You finished 142.5 at the top of the range and got 150 for fourteen on 2 August, up from 150 for eleven two weeks earlier, so 142.5 has nothing left to give and both sets move to 150. Fifteen on both is what buys the next step to 157.5.

Both sets hit fifteen at 97.5 on 2 August, the top of the range, which earns the 7.5-lb step to 105. Twelve is the honest landing after a jump - last time you stepped up here you came back down to thirteen and twelve before climbing again.

You stepped up to 135 on 2 August and got twelve and twelve, the bottom of the range, so the weight holds and the reps move by one. The card would ask fifteen twice, a three-rep jump on both sets in one night.

You carried 300 for three sets of twelve on 16 August, so 300 is the right pin - but the card copies that night forward and asks fifteen on all three, three more per set than you have ever done at this weight. The next leg-press pin is 320 and it only opens once 300 goes for fifteen.

Three sets of fifteen at 55 on 2 August earned the 5-lb step, and you took 60 for three sets of twelve on 16 August - reprinting 60 for twelve is an exact copy of that night and asks for nothing new. One more rep per set is the smallest real step, and fifteens across the board buy 65.

This is bodyweight, so reps are the only thing that can move, and you have opened with twelve and twelve in every leg session since 18 July because the card reprints twelve every time. Thirteen is the step, and the range now runs to fifteen.
